en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on Ants.
5. The Question of the Mongoose “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one quality of the mongoose should be adopted,’ which is that one quality that should be adopted?
“Great King, just as a mongoose, when approaching a snake, approaches it after having fortified its body with medicine in order to seize the snake;”

In the same way, Great King, a yogi practicing yoga who approaches a world overcome by anger, resentment, strife, quarrels, disputes, and opposition, should anoint his mind with the medicinal ointment of loving-kindness (*mettā*).
This, Great King, is one quality of the mongoose that should be adopted.
And this, Great King, was said by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:
"Therefore, one should cultivate loving-kindness for oneself and for others;
one should pervade all with a mind of loving-kindness."
“This is the teaching of the Buddhas.
Thus ends the fifth question, that of Nakulaṅga.
